options.name: Emma Long Metropolitan Park (The Grove primitive sites)
options.priceNote: $10/night primitive walk-in tent site (Grove or Bluff); utility sites $20-25. City of Austin park.
options.locationNote: 1600 City Park Rd on Lake Austin — significantly off-route, ~12 road miles NW of the downtown/Zilker endpoint, hilly approach
options.legalityNote: Official City of Austin campground; online reservation required (up to 180 days ahead)
options.cyclistIntel: Cheapest legal tent spot in Austin metro, but the detour NW up City Park Rd is long and steep with a loaded bike — only worth it if you want two nights in Austin
options.seasonalNote: Thu 8 Oct 2026; October weekends fill, weeknight usually fine but reserve

options.name: McKinney Falls State Park
options.priceNote: $20/night 30-amp water+electric site ($24 for 50-amp) PLUS $6/person/day TPWD entrance fee — solo total ~$26
options.locationNote: 5808 McKinney Falls Pkwy, SE Austin — ~7 mi from downtown endpoint, close to the inbound route from Bastrop, so easiest hit on the way IN
options.legalityNote: Texas State Park; reserve at texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com
options.cyclistIntel: Standard ST-rider choice for Austin — quiet, showers, and you skip downtown chaos; ride the 7 mi into town unloaded next morning
options.seasonalNote: Thursday night in October usually available, but Austin parks book up around festival weekends — reserve ahead

options.name: Firehouse Hostel (downtown Austin)
options.priceNote: Dorm beds from ~$29 (typically $29-45 by night); private rooms from ~$99. Indoor bed, not camping.
options.locationNote: 605 Brazos St, downtown — ~0.7 mi from the Day 18 endpoint near Zilker/downtown
options.legalityNote: Commercial hostel in Austin's 1885 fire station; 24-hour desk
options.cyclistIntel: Largest hostel in Texas and the practical budget indoor option; secure your bike inside/ask staff
options.seasonalNote: ACL Festival is traditionally the first two October weekends at Zilker — Oct 8-9 likely collides with fest weekend 2; dorm prices spike and sell out, book well ahead

gapAdvice: Pecan Grove RV Park (0.2 mi off, Barton Springs Rd) is RVs ONLY — no tents, sites to $80, so skip it. HI Austin (Lakeshore Blvd) no longer appears in current listings and is believed permanently closed — Firehouse Hostel is the working hostel fallback. Warning: ACL Fest (typically Oct weekends 1-2 at Zilker, i.e. right at your Oct 8 arrival) jacks up every downtown bed — camp at McKinney Falls to stay insulated.

options.name: Pedernales Falls State Park
options.priceNote: $20/night water+electric site (69 sites) PLUS $6/person/day entrance — solo ~$26. Hike-in primitive is $10 but sits 2 mi down a rough trail (impractical with a loaded touring bike).
options.locationNote: ~9-10 road miles NE of Johnson City: turn off US-290 east of town onto FM 3232 / Park Rd 6026 before reaching JC, or backtrack from town
options.legalityNote: Texas State Park; reserve online via Texas State Parks reservation system
options.cyclistIntel: The only real budget camp near Johnson City now that the in-town RV parks have gone RV-only; showers, good facilities, swimming in the Pedernales
options.seasonalNote: Friday night 9 Oct — Hill Country state parks fill on fall weekends; reserve as soon as dates firm

options.name: Miller Creek RV Park
options.priceNote: $52-62/night per aggregator listings — over budget, but tents are explicitly welcomed; call for a solo-tent rate, small parks often quote less
options.locationNote: 5618 US-281 S, ~4-5 mi south of Johnson City (OSM pegs it at route mile 1123.4, on the line)
options.legalityNote: Private commercial RV park that advertises tent camping
options.cyclistIntel: Fallback if you don't want the Pedernales Falls detour; showers, laundry, store on site

gapAdvice: Johnson City proper is now a tent DESERT: Roadrunner RV Park (mi 1119.2, the old ST standby) is RV/cabin only (30A from $45, cabins $65, no tents per its own site), Johnson City RV Park is a $70-80 'boutique' RV-only park, and Flat Creek Crossing Ranch (mi 1101.6) has SUSPENDED all tent/RV camping until further notice. LBJ National Historical Park and LBJ State Park (Stonewall) are day-use, no camping. Practical plan: reserve Pedernales Falls and peel off before town, or budget-bust at Miller Creek. Cash-strapped riders have historically asked at JC churches — unverified, ask locally, never assume.

options.name: Kerrville-Schreiner Park
options.priceNote: $25/night tent site (official city rate page); RV 30A water-only $35, full hookups $40-50. Some sources cite a $6/person entry fee on top — confirm when booking. City adds 3.5% surcharge on card payments (since Oct 2025).
options.locationNote: 2385 Bandera Hwy (TX-173), on the Guadalupe ~3 mi SE of downtown Kerrville endpoint
options.legalityNote: City of Kerrville park (517-acre former state park); tent areas in Riverside, Fox Run Loop, Fawn Hideaway
options.cyclistIntel: THE classic Southern Tier stop in Kerrville — decades of ST journals and local bike-tour groups (about half of Easter Hill Country Tour riders) camp here; river swimming, showers, town services 3 mi away
options.seasonalNote: Saturday night 10 Oct on a fall holiday weekend — reserve online ahead rather than rolling in

options.name: Johnson Creek RV Resort & Park (Ingram)
options.priceNote: Tent camping listed as available but nightly tent rate unpublished — estimate $30-45, call to confirm
options.locationNote: Junction Hwy (TX-27/39 corridor) west of Ingram, ~7-8 route miles PAST Kerrville — position approximate
options.legalityNote: Private RV resort that accepts tent campers per listings
options.cyclistIntel: Useful if you want to bank miles past Kerrville toward Hunt; verify tent policy by phone first

gapAdvice: The RV-park cluster on the OSM hints is mostly useless for tents: Buckhorn Lake Resort and Guadalupe River RV Resort are big-rig luxury resorts, and Take-It-Easy (mi 1182.4) is a 55+ RV community — none confirm tents. Kerrville-Schreiner is the obvious answer; book the Saturday night early.

options.name: Lost Maples State Natural Area — primitive hike-in sites
options.priceNote: $10/night + $6/person entrance (solo ~$16). CAUTION: sites are a 1-3.2 mi hike from parking on steep rough trails, no potable water, no fires — awkward to impossible with a loaded touring bike
options.locationNote: Entrance on RM 187 north of Vanderpool; camping areas roughly 1.3-2.6 mi off the route line
options.legalityNote: TPWD natural area; reservation via Texas State Parks system
options.cyclistIntel: Cheapest on paper but you'd have to stash/push the bike down hiking trails — most riders take the developed loop or the private campground instead
options.seasonalNote: Peak-crowd season starts in October; park closes entry when parking lots (250 cars) fill on color weekends

options.name: Lost Maples RV and Camping (private)
options.priceNote: $15/night primitive tent site (10 sites, no hookups); $24/night to pitch on an RV site with water+electric. 24-hour restrooms and showers.
options.locationNote: 33557 RM 187 at Vanderpool, 0.1 mi off the route right at the day's endpoint
options.cyclistIntel: The zero-detour, no-lottery option at Vanderpool — showers included at half the SNA's developed-site cost; call ahead in October
options.seasonalNote: Fall-color overflow from the SNA lands here — phone ahead for the holiday weekend

options.name: Lost Maples State Natural Area — campsites with electricity
options.priceNote: $20/night (30 sites, water+30A) + $6/person entrance — solo ~$26; showers in nearby restrooms
options.locationNote: Developed loop near park HQ on RM 187, ~2-3 mi off route north of Vanderpool
options.cyclistIntel: Iconic overnight if you can get a site — maple canyon trails at your tent flap
options.seasonalNote: CRITICAL: arrival is Sun 11 Oct 2026 — the Columbus Day long weekend and the front edge of leaf season. The 30 developed sites sell out far ahead on Oct/Nov weekends (bookable ~5 months out); reserve IMMEDIATELY or stalk cancellations. A Sunday night is your best shot vs Fri/Sat.

gapAdvice: Foxfire Cabins (1 mi S of the SNA on the Sabinal) is cabins-only — no tent sites — and runs multi-night minimums in leaf season; treat as a splurge/bad-weather bail only. If everything at Vanderpool is somehow full, Utopia (~16 mi south, off route) has lodging, and Leakey (17 mi ahead over the big 337 climbs) has commercial camps — but on a Sunday night the private Lost Maples RV almost certainly has a $15 primitive spot; call (830) 966-3912 a few days out.

options.name: Wes Cooksey Park (Uvalde County)
options.priceNote: ~$16/night camping (last verified rate, 2022) + $4/person day-use fee; current price unconfirmed — call (830) 597-3223
options.locationNote: 33719 TX-55 on the Nueces at Camp Wood, 0.1 mi off route (OSM mi 1277.2) — position approximate
options.legalityNote: County-run public park with RV and tent camping and river swimming; showers not confirmed
options.cyclistIntel: Cheap public option right on the line entering Camp Wood; Camp Wood is a canonical ST overnight before the notoriously hard 36 westbound miles
options.seasonalNote: Monday night 12 Oct (Columbus Day) — summer river crowds long gone, space near-certain

options.name: Nueces River RV and Cabin Resort (formerly Big Oak River Camp)
options.priceNote: Tent sites WITH water+electric; current rates not published online (legacy listings said ~$15) — book via bookings.rmscloud.com or call (830) 597-5280
options.locationNote: 32598 TX-55, 0.3 mi off route at the day's endpoint (OSM mi 1278.3)
options.legalityNote: Established private campground; note old domain bigoakrivercamp.com is dead — it rebranded
options.cyclistIntel: This is the 'Big Oak River Camp' of countless ST journals — shaded oak/pecan tent sites a short walk from the Nueces, bathhouses, pool, camp store, laundry

options.name: Los Rios Campground
options.priceNote: 10 tent sites (1-5 with water+electric, 6-10 primitive); rates only shown in their ResNexus booking engine — expect $20-35
options.locationNote: 751 River Rd on the Nueces, ~4 route miles before Camp Wood (OSM mi 1273.9) — position approximate
options.legalityNote: Established private campground (14 acres, cabins/tiny homes/RV/tent); men's & women's bathhouses
options.cyclistIntel: Newer, well-reviewed river campground if the two in-town options don't pan out

bestBet: Nueces River RV and Cabin Resort (formerly Big Oak River Camp)
gapAdvice: Camp Wood remains one of the friendliest cheap-camping towns on the Texas ST — three legal riverfront options within 4 miles. Resupply and top off water here: the next day westward is the famously brutal, service-free stretch toward Brackettville/Del Rio.

options.name: Amistad NRA — 277 North Campground
options.priceNote: $6-10/night NPS fee (50% off with Senior/Access pass); NO potable water, vault toilet, covered picnic table + grill
options.locationNote: Off US-277 ~9 mi north of downtown Del Rio (a detour spur, not on the ST line) — position approximate
options.legalityNote: National Park Service campground, first-come first-served, no reservations
options.cyclistIntel: Dirt-cheap federal camping, but the 277 spur adds off-route miles — Governors Landing usually makes more sense for through-riders
options.seasonalNote: Tue 13 Oct — FCFS is low-risk on a weekday in October

options.name: Amistad NRA — Governors Landing Campground
options.priceNote: $6-10/night NPS fee; the ONLY Amistad campground with drinking water (shared spigots); vault toilets, no showers, no ground fires
options.locationNote: Off US-90 W at the reservoir near Amistad Dam, ~12 route miles past the Day 23 endpoint / ~8 mi past downtown Del Rio — position approximate
options.legalityNote: National Park Service campground, first-come first-served, 14-day max
options.cyclistIntel: Long-standing ST bargain stop — banks miles toward Comstock and puts you lakeside; carry dinner/breakfast from Del Rio since there are no services
options.seasonalNote: Weekday in October = sites open; sunset over the reservoir is the payoff

options.name: Hidden Valley RV Park (Del Rio)
options.priceNote: Tent camping ~$20/night per directory listings (10% Good Sam discount cited); rate unverified — call ahead
options.locationNote: Older shaded district of Del Rio, ~8 mi past the endpoint on the route through town (OSM mi 1354.7) — position approximate
options.legalityNote: Private in-town RV park; laundromat on site
options.cyclistIntel: In-town option if you want groceries, restaurants, and a real shower before the desert stretch

options.name: Fort Clark Springs (Brackettville) — behind-route fallback
options.priceNote: Tent camping listed at roughly $15-35/night, 2-person base +$1/extra person; COLD showers at tent area; RV full-hookup ~$40
options.locationNote: Historic fort/member resort at Brackettville — ~30 route miles BEFORE the Day 23 endpoint, so it's a stop-short option, not a same-day one
options.legalityNote: Private association resort that sells overnight camping to travelers; spring-fed pool
options.cyclistIntel: Classic ST split-the-difference stop: if 68 mi Camp Wood→Laughlin is too big a day, sleep here and re-plan Del Rio as a short morning

options.name: Lonesome Dove RV Ranch
options.priceNote: $22/night daily rate (weekly $135); tent policy NOT confirmed — sites are electric RV-style, phone first
options.locationNote: US-90 W beyond Del Rio toward Amistad (OSM mi 1359.9) — position approximate
options.legalityNote: Private RV park; treat tentsOk as unknown-leaning-no until confirmed by phone
options.cyclistIntel: Only worth a call if Governors Landing is somehow full

gapAdvice: The mapped endpoint sits by Laughlin AFB, and the FamCamp there is restricted to military/DoD ID holders (active, guard, reserve, retired, DAV, DoD civilians) — EXCLUDED for a civilian rider, and there is no other camping at that exact point. Real choices: (a) push 8-12 extra miles through Del Rio to Hidden Valley (~$20, town services) or on to Amistad's Governors Landing ($6-10, water on site, FCFS, no showers); (b) stop 30 mi short at Fort Clark Springs; or (c) motel row in Del Rio. Whatever you pick, leave Del Rio with maximum water — Amistad campgrounds other than Governors Landing are dry, and so is the road to Comstock.
